# Adding an item or an interactable

Items live in the pack; interactables (`ResourceKind`) stand in the world and are gathered or
cleared into items. Both are simulation data first. Read `docs/architecture.md` sections 4, 5 and 8,
and the `homestead-code-conventions` skill. Worked examples: `WildGarlic` (forageable flower and
item) and `BrambleBank` (clearable overgrowth).

## A. A new item

1. **Enum:** append to `Homestead::Item` in `Simulation/HomesteadItems.h`, just before `Count`,
   under a comment naming your OpenSpec change. Never reorder or remove values.
2. **Catalogue row:** add the matching row to `ItemCatalogue` in `Simulation/HomesteadItems.cpp`,
   in the same position: stable `key` (kebab-case, never shown, never changed), display `name`,
   one-sentence `description`, `ItemCategory`, `icon` glyph key, `basePriceCents`, buyer mask
   (`StoreBuys` / `NoBuyers`), `hunger`/`energy` if edible, `source` text for recipe hints, and
   `plural` if "3 <name>s" reads wrong. The build fails if the row count doesn't match the enum.
3. **Icon:** add the glyph in `UI/SHomesteadIcon.{h,cpp}`: an `EKind` value, the key→kind entry in
   the lookup table, and a `case` in the painter. Reuse an existing glyph with a new tint if no
   drawing is needed yet.
4. **Where it comes from:** a yield (`Yield` in `HomesteadSimulation.cpp`, or an `OgGives` in
   `HomesteadOvergrowth.cpp`), a recipe (`Recipe` enum + `RecipeName` + `CraftChange`), a shop's
   stock (`HomesteadShops.cpp`), or a grant.
5. **Hotbar:** tools and food can be pinned (`AHomesteadController::CanPinToHotbar`). A new tool
   also needs its `ToolKind` mapping, held-mesh attachment in `AHomesteadCharacter` and an action
   animation (skill `homestead-animation-layer`).
6. **Saves:** nothing to do. Stocks are saved with their width (version 13), so older saves load
   with your item at zero. Never reorder or remove items; that does break saves.
7. **Tests:** extend `Tests/HomesteadSimulationTests.cpp` or `Tests/HomesteadEconomyTests.cpp`
   (catalogue lookups, yield, price, recipe). Run `Scripts\Test-Native.ps1 -Configuration Release`.
8. **Editor play tools:** if agents need to name it from Python, the item key already works
   (`ItemFromKey`); nothing else to add.

## B. A new interactable kind

1. **Enum:** append to `Homestead::ResourceKind` in `Simulation/HomesteadSimulation.h` before
   `Count`, and its display name to `ResourceName` in `HomesteadSimulation.cpp` (same order;
   guarded by `static_assert`).
2. **Rules**, one of:
   - *Forageable and regrowing* (berries, flowers): a `Regrowth` hours case and a `Yield` case in
     `HomesteadSimulation.cpp`.
   - *Cleared with a tool* (overgrowth, stumps, rocks): one `OgTable` row in
     `HomesteadOvergrowth.cpp`: tool, whether it can be done by hand, minimum `ToolTier`, energy,
     swings per tier, yields (`OgGives(item, low, high, chance)`).
3. **Visual:** a `case` in `AHomesteadWorld::BuildOvergrowth` (clearables) or `BuildResource`
   (forageables) in `HomesteadWorld.cpp`, loading
   `/Game/SurvivalGame/Environment/Props/<Folder>/SM_<Name>`. Author the mesh with a Blender recipe
   (`blender-assets` skill) and import it with `import_props.py`. A missing mesh logs an error and
   fails the refresh, so land the asset with the code.
4. **Prompt and actions:** the focus title comes from `ResourceName`; the verb and the required tool
   come from the rules above, so most kinds need no controller change. Only a new *kind of action*
   needs controller work (`UpdateFocus`, `FocusActions`, `Interact`/`UseSelectedTool`).
5. **Editor play tools:** add the name to the `ResourceKind` switch in
   `Source/SurvivalGameEditor/HomesteadAgentPlayLibrary.cpp` so agents can find it.
6. **Tests:** a native test that the node yields what you expect (and, for clearables, the tier
   gate and swing count).

## C. Placing interactables on the Estate

- **Claim an id range first** on the round page (`docs/handoff/round-<n>.md`, "Registry: estate
  placement ids") through the docs agent or orchestrator, and update the range comment in
  `Simulation/HomesteadEstate.h`. Ids live in `[500000, 1000000)` and must never be reused: a save
  stores cleared placements by id.
- **Many placements:** generate them with a script under `Scripts/Terrain/` that writes a
  `Simulation/HomesteadEstate<Name>Placements.inc` headed "Generated by ...; do not edit by hand",
  and include it from `ProvisionalEstatePlacements()` in `HomesteadEstate.cpp`
  (see `scatter.py` → `HomesteadEstateWorldPlacements.inc`). Generators must assign the same id to
  the same placement on every run. **Never compact accepted candidates:** a newly rejected forage or
  terrain candidate must not shift every later id. Freeze an id -> kind -> position manifest, preserve
  skipped/reserved candidate slots, and add a regeneration test that proves existing placement ids
  remain byte-for-byte stable before rebaking/merging.
- **A few hand-placed ones:** add them in `HomesteadEstate.cpp` next to the existing `along(...)`
  and anchor-relative placements. `grow(...)` and `along(...)` number placements sequentially
  (`next++`), so **only append at the end of a run**: inserting a line in the middle renumbers every
  later placement, and saves then mark the wrong nodes cleared.
- Keep them off roads, water and buildings; `scatter.py` hides decorative scenery around every
  resource automatically.
- Adding new ids is save-compatible. Moving, removing or renumbering existing ones isn't: that needs
  `table.bakeVersion` in `ProvisionalEstatePlacements()` raised, which makes older estate saves
  refuse to load with a "start a new game" message. Ask the orchestrator, like a save-version bump.

## Done when

- Native tests all pass, the editor module builds, and in PIE you can walk up to it, see the
  right prompt, act on it with the right tool and get the right items (a `shot` capture of the
  prompt and the pack is the evidence).
